summary: two independent transient WinError 5 partial applies in the real project inside one unattended session, plus a deterministic reproduction in a scratch project

incidents.settled_by: saipen recover inspect -> recover resolve --resolution accept_live (NEEDS_REPAIR) -> --resolution replan (NEEDS_REPAIR) -> bare saipen recover (RECOVERED)

incidents.when: 2026-10-02T06:0xZ, minutes later, in the same session
incidents.settled_by: bare saipen recover (RECOVERED) -- which ROLLED THE FINISH FORWARD: the command had just refused, and the recovery completed the very operation the refusal named
incidents.consequence: T-1399 ended up closed and the project phase reached DONE without the agent re-issuing ticket done

recurrence_measured.what_ran_concurrently_on_this_machine: a separate SAIPEN session writing its own project memory under V:\___VAC\__K\__CODE\_AI_STUFF_AGENTIC\_SAIPEN\.saipen, and an antivirus/search indexer is the usual Windows cause
recurrence_measured.significance: T-1394's recurrence field says 'any Windows process holding a short lock on .saipen/LOG.md'. The measurement widens it: it is not LOG.md-specific, it is not once-per-machine, and it fires without any human touching the machine. The agent recovered both times by knowing the unadvertised route, which is a fact about my memory, not about the protocol.

incident_2_is_the_stronger_form_of_t1400.claim: a bare `saipen recover` settles a CONFLICT that `saipen recover resolve` refuses, contradicting OPS.md
incident_2_is_the_stronger_form_of_t1400.incident_1: the bare recover reconciled a last_event counter, which is a repair
incident_2_is_the_stronger_form_of_t1400.incident_2: the bare recover ROLLED A REFUSED OPERATION FORWARD to its intended end state -- not a repair of bookkeeping but the completion of a write the agent was told had failed
incident_2_is_the_stronger_form_of_t1400.why_that_is_worse: a tool result of `REFUSE [CONFLICT]` is an answer. An agent that obeys it will stop and report the block. The tree then moves anyway, silently. Nothing in the LOG line the recovery wrote says which resolution class was applied, because none was: OPS.md's roll-forward path is not a resolution class at all.

state_after_both.validate: CURRENT_FAIL with exactly 1 problem -- the pre-existing sweep-ticket-link ledger entry -- and 66 warnings, i.e. no residue from either incident

not_proven: which process took each lock; Windows does not attribute this without an audit subscription, and none is available here
that a retry inside the engine would have succeeded within a reasonable bound -- the lock is released by the time the agent re-issues the command, which is why the manual recovery works at all
